newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Beijing Yanhua seen in HK$1.8-2.3 bln H-shr float.
newsitem.headline: Beijing Yanhua seen in HK$1.8-2.3 bln H-shr float.

text.p: Beijing Yanhua Petrochemcial Co Ltd is expected to raise HK$1.79 billion to HK$2.30 billion through a dual listing in Hong Kong and New York, to cut debt and to expand production, analysts said on Thursday.
Beijing Yanhua is expected to issue 1.012 billion H-shares, or 30 percent of the company's enlarged share capital, at a price ranging from HK$1.77 to HK$2.27 per share, analysts said.
H-shares are Hong Kong-listed shares in Chinese enterprises.
"The issue price will represent a P/E (price to earnings) multiple of 11.6 to 15 times on a fully-diluted basis," said one analyst after attended a company presentation on Thursday.

Of the total, 455.4 million shares is expected to be offered to the U.S. market, another 455.4 million shares will be placed internationally and 101.2 million shares will be earmarked for public subscription in Hong Kong, analysts said.
"The company will seek a listing in the U.S. through ADRs (American Depository Receipts). Each ADR will represent 50 company shares," another analyst said.
Analysts said Beijing Yanhua was also expected to grant underwriters an option to require it to issue up to an additional 151.8 million shares to cover over-allotment.
The Hong Kong public offer is expected to run from June 17 to 20 and dealing in the shares is expected to begin on June 24 in New York and on June 25 in Hong Kong, they said.
SBC Warburg and Bear Stearns are expected to be the global co-ordinators of the issue.
Beijing Yanhua, locating in the Beijing suburbs, is a resins and plastics producer in China.

The company aims to increase its production capacity of resin and plastics, synthetic rubber and basic organic chemicals by about 83 percent to 2.12 million tonnes by the year 2000, from the current 1.16 million tonnes, analysts said.
Net proceeds to be raised from the issue is expected to be used to cut debt and to expand production capacity, they said.
Beijing Yanhua posted profit of 530.5 million yuan for the year ended in December 1996, compared with 815.1 million yuan in 1995 and 178.2 million yuan in 1994.
Turnover was 5.98 billion yuan in 1996, against 6.99 billion yuan in 1995 and 3.48 billion yuan in 1994.
